photos.caption: First Capitol of the Republic of Texas (1837-1882) - National Capitol of the Republic of Texas (1837-1839). Built rapidly in early 1837 by Augustus C. and John Kirby Allen after the Texas Congress named Houston the temporary capital of the Republic of Texas, this two-story milled-pine structure hosted President Sam Houston, Mirabeau B. Lamar, and the First through Third Congresses before the capital moved to Austin in 1839. It later operated as the Old Capitol Hotel until 1882.
photos.attribution: Wikimedia Commons / Dudley G. Wooten (1898)

photos.address: 909 Texas Ave at Main St (NW Corner, Block 57)
photos.caption: The Capitol Hotel (1883) (1883-1912) - Grand Victorian Hotel on the Republic Capitol Site. Designed by Houston architect George E. Dickey and opened in April 1883 on the exact footprint of the 1837 Republic Capitol, the five-story brick Capitol Hotel was Houston's premier Victorian hostelry. Acquired by William Marsh Rice and renamed the Rice Hotel after an 1890s annex addition, it was demolished by Jesse H. Jones in 1912 to erect the extant 18-story Rice Hotel.

photos.caption: Victorian City Hall & Market House (1871 / 1876) (1876-1901) - Twin-Towered Brick Municipal Market & Opera House on Market Square. After the 1871 brick City Hall & Market House burned in 1876, Houstonians immediately rebuilt a nearly identical High Victorian brick landmark on the same foundations, complete with a grand upstairs Market Opera House and twin ornate towers. Displayed prominently in the 1885, 1890, and 1896 Sanborn Atlases, it burned in June 1901.

photos.address: 1001 Texas Ave at Main St (NE Corner, Block 56)
photos.caption: The Binz Building (1895) (1895-1951) - Houston's First Six-Story Office Skyscraper with Electric Elevator. Commissioned by Jacob Binz and designed by Olle J. Lorehn in 1895 on the northeast corner of Main Street and Texas Avenue (directly across Main Street from the Capitol Hotel, on the exact site of the modern 1001 Texas Avenue Binz Building), the six-story Binz Building was hailed as Houston's first skyscraper. For more than half a century its upper floors housed the consular corps and early oil wildcatters after Spindletop.

photos.address: 6900 Main St at W. Holcombe Blvd
photos.caption: The Shamrock Hotel (1949) (1949-1987) - Glenn McCarthy's 18-Story International Style Resort & Olympic Pool. Opened by wildcatter Glenn McCarthy on St. Patrick's Day 1949 in a Hollywood gala broadcast nationwide, the 1,100-room Shamrock Hotel featured green-tinted interiors, the Emerald Room supper club, and the world's largest outdoor hotel swimming pool (165 by 142 feet, large enough for water skiing). Its 1987 demolition galvanized Houston's modern historic preservation movement.
photos.attribution: Wikimedia Commons / 1950 Shamrock Hotel Postcard

photos.caption: The Majestic Theatre (1923) (1923-1971) - World's First 'Atmospheric' Movie Palace by Architect John Eberson. Opened on January 29, 1923 for Karl Hoblitzelle's Interstate Circuit, Houston's 2,200-seat Majestic Theatre was the very first 'atmospheric' movie palace in world architectural history. Architect John Eberson created a plaster Mediterranean courtyard beneath a cobalt dome with projected moving clouds, twinkling stars, and stuffed peacocks.
